verdict.rationale: Community users confirm Logseq keeps notes as local markdown/org files they can version in git, sync with Syncthing, and read in other tools such as Emacs/org-agenda (logseq-comm-10, logseq-comm-20, logseq-comm-7, logseq-comm-8). The docs say sync is opt-in per graph, so some graphs can stay local-only (logseq-docs-40), and full-graph export to standard Markdown exists (logseq-docs-30). However, the newer DB version reportedly stops keeping data as markdown files (logseq-comm-15), and users describe the file formats as non-standard and say the app rewrites files by stripping blank lines (logseq-comm-17, logseq-comm-12). missing for 10: first-party documentation of the on-disk file format and of fully offline operation, and clarity on whether the DB version keeps notes readable without the app.
